question.problem:
A travel agency offers three itineraries, itinerary $1,$ itinerary $2,$ and itinerary $3.$ For each itinerary, customers can decide to travel using their own car or the agency's bus.

- Itinerary $1$ is chosen by $60%$ of the customers, and $10%$ of those customers travel by bus.

- Itinerary $2$ is chosen by $20%$ of the customers, and $25%$ of those customers travel by bus.

- Itinerary $3$ is chosen by $20%$ of the customers.

If $30%$ of all customers travel with children, $50%$ of customers with children choose the bus, and $83%$ of customers that choose the bus travel with children, what is the probability that a randomly chosen customer that chooses itinerary $3$ takes the bus? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be the event that a customer has children, $B$ be the event that a customer takes the bus, and ${I}_{1},{I}_{2},{I}_{3}$ be the event that a customer chooses itinerary $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively. 

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

- From the bullet points, we have the following information:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P({I}_{1})=0.6 &  & P(B|{I}_{1})=0.1 \\  & P({I}_{2})=0.2 &  & P(B|{I}_{2})=0.25 \\  & P({I}_{3})=0.2\end{aligned}
$$

The disjoint union ${I}_{1}⊔{I}_{2}⊔{I}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space, and we have

$$
P({I}_{1})+P({I}_{2})+P({I}_{3})=0.6+0.2+0.2=1.
$$

- Since $30%$ of customers have children, we have

$$
P(C)=0.3.
$$

- Since $50%$ of customers with children choose the bus, we have

$$
P(B|C)=0.5.
$$

- Since $83%$ of customers that choose the bus have children, we have

$$
P(C|B)=0.83.
$$

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen customer that chooses itinerary $3$ travels by bus, which is represented as $P(B|{I}_{3}).$ 

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(C|B) & =\frac{P(B|C)P(C)}{P(B)} \\ P(C|B) & =\frac{P(B|C)P(C)}{P(B|{I}_{1})P({I}_{1})+P(B|{I}_{2})P({I}_{2})+P(B|{I}_{3})P({I}_{3})} \\ 0.83 & =\frac{(0.5)(0.3)}{(0.1)(0.6)+(0.25)(0.2)+P(B|{I}_{3})(0.2)} \\ 0.83 & =\frac{0.15}{0.11+0.2P(B|{I}_{3})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation for $P(B|{I}_{3}),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.83(0.11+0.2P(B|{I}_{3})) & =0.15 \\ 0.11+0.2P(B|{I}_{3}) & =\frac{0.15}{0.83} \\ 0.11+0.2P(B|{I}_{3}) & =\frac{15}{83} \\ 0.2P(B|{I}_{3}) & =\frac{15}{83}-0.11 \\ P(B|{I}_{3}) & =\frac{1}{0.2}(\frac{15}{83}-0.11) \\ P(B|{I}_{3}) & ≈0.354\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
